paper_title: dKV-Cache The Cache for Diffusion Language Models
caption: Impact of batch size on decoding speed. Evaluated on LLaDA with a single NVIDIA H20; prefill length fixed at 100 tokens.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how decoding throughput (Token/s) varies with batch size for four sequence lengths (L = 16, 32, 64, 128), showing two decoding modes (dKV-Cache-Decode vs Origin) on the same axes. The x-axis is labeled “Batch Size,” uses a linear scale, spans approximately 0 to 130, and shows regularly spaced numeric ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120, with plotted batch sizes appearing at discrete values up to 128. The y-axis is labeled “Token/s,” uses a linear scale, spans 0 to 225, and has regularly spaced tick marks every 25 tokens/s. There are eight lines total, with color/marker indicating L and line style indicating mode: for L=16 a light-gray line with square markers, for L=32 a blue line with circular markers, for L=64 a red line with upward-triangle markers, and for L=128 a dark navy line with downward-triangle markers; dKV-Cache-Decode is shown with solid lines while Origin is shown with dashed lines. For dKV-Cache-Decode (solid), the light-gray L=16 line increases across the batch sizes, reaching labeled values of 173.17 at batch size 32, 189.74 at 64, and 202.31 at 128; the blue L=32 solid line rises to 159.24 at batch size 32, then to 175.95 at 64 and 183.28 at 128; the red L=64 solid line reaches 119.55 at 32, 126.86 at 64, and 130.58 at 128; and the dark navy L=128 solid line reaches 75.72 at 32, 78.76 at 64, and 81.18 at 128.
